summary: High-density workstation kitting: mislabeled PSU, customs hold, and badge reprovision needed
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple new high-density workstation kits arrived at the London office packing station with power supplies (PSUs) labeled for 110V regions. The kits are destined for eu-west desks and cannot be completed until correct 230V PSUs are installed. At least one pallet is currently flagged in customs due to a mismatch between the commercial invoice and the SKU descriptions. Additionally, vendor techs scheduled to complete desk assembly tomorrow require temporary building access; their badges were provisioned under a different vendor umbrella and currently fail SSO validation.

Impact:
- 12 desks in the LDN hub cannot be completed for new hires scheduled next week (onboarding delay).
- Customs hold prevents additional kits (3 pallets) from being released; risk of extended lead time and billing hold.
- Vendor technicians cannot complete on-site assembly without badge reprovision or escorted access.

Environment:
- Site: Redwood London Facility (6th Floor, Dock 3)
- Shipment carrier: DHL Express tracking 3629EUX12345
- Kit batch: KTN-2026-HDD-42, manifest v3

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) Receiving team attempted to match PSUs to kit packing list during kitting QA on 2026-03-09 09:10 GMT.
2) Found 18/18 PSUs stamped "110V" inside boxes labeled for EU deployment.
3) Receiving created hold and notified Procurement + Facilities.
4) Carrier reported a customs inquiry citing invoice SKU mismatch at 2026-03-09 14:35 GMT.
5) Vendor tech badges were scheduled to be activated on 2026-03-11 but report SSO provisioning failure when checking in at front desk.

Logs / Evidence:
- DHL tracking page snapshot: https://dhl.example/track/3629EUX12345 (internal view)
- Photos of PSU labels and packing list: https://s3.internal.redwood/uploads/INT-550123/photos.zip
- Commercial invoice copy uploaded to ticket attachments
comments: 2026-03-10 08:22 - Jamal Ortiz (Facilities): Received initial report from Receiving. I visited Dock 3 and confirmed all PSUs in box 7 and 9 are labeled 110V. I tagged the pallet as HOLD and stopped kitting. Reached out to Procurement for PO and vendor confirmation.

2026-03-10 09:05 - Lina Chen (Procurement): Vendor (HWGlobal Ltd) confirms packing error on batch KTN-2026-HDD-42; they will overnight ship replacement 230V PSUs from their EU warehouse, ETA 2026-03-11 16:00 GMT. Provided RMA number RMA-98721 for return of incorrect units.

2026-03-10 11:47 - Customs Liaison (Shipping): Customs put the second pallet on documentation hold because line-item descriptions on the commercial invoice use internal SKUs instead of harmonized commodity descriptions. I filed amendment request with DHL and uploaded corrected invoice. Awaiting clearance update.

2026-03-11 07:30 - Jamie Park (Security Ops): Vendor tech badges failing SSO validation because vendor identity provider mapping changed last week. I can temporarily reprovision escorted guest badges for the scheduled techs; request Facilities confirmation for escort window.

2026-03-12 09:12 - Priya Malhotra (Reporter): Confirming we need temporary escorted access 2026-03-12 13:00-17:00 to complete desks ahead of Monday onboarding. Also request Procurement to confirm whether vendor will prepay any customs fees for amendment delay.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: packing/labeling error at vendor produced wrong PSUs; commercial invoice used internal SKUs which triggered customs documentation review. Confirmed vendor acknowledgement and RMA. Tracking shows replacement PSUs dispatched from DE hub (DHL AWB 3629EUX67890). Customs amendment filed against AWB 3629EUX12345; clearance pending — portal ticket #CUST-4452. Asset tags on affected kits: ASSET-LDN-HT-0001..0012. Photos of labels indicate physical 110V printed sticker; serials match vendor manifest but not description strings in invoice. Temporary options considered: (1) swap PSUs on site when replacements arrive; (2) request loaner 230V PSUs from London spares (inventory shows 10 compatible units under SPARE-230V-LDN). Chosen path: use 6 spares to complete highest-priority desks and wait for vendor shipment for the remainder. Badge issue root cause: vendor SSO mapping change; Security Ops can issue escorted guest passes for the techs for a 4-hour window.
resolution: Workaround implemented 2026-03-12: Facilities used 6 spare 230V PSUs from local spares pool to complete 6 high-priority desks. Vendor shipped replacement 230V PSUs (AWB 3629EUX67890) and DHL updated customs with corrected invoice; pallets released from customs 2026-03-12 15:40 GMT. Incorrect 110V PSUs placed on RMA RMA-98721 and scheduled for return pickup by vendor on 2026-03-14. Security Ops reprovisioned escorted guest passes for vendor techs for 2026-03-12 13:00-17:00, allowing assembly to complete. Follow-ups: Procurement to update vendor packing checklist to include harmonized descriptions (action item: PROC-asset-checklist-update, due 2026-03-19), Facilities to perform inventory reconciliation of spare PSUs and increase EU spare pool to 20 units (action item: FAC-SPARE-2026-03). Postmortem: schedule retrospective with Procurement, Receiving, and Vendor Ops to prevent recurrence.
actions: Procurement to update vendor packing checklist and require harmonized commodity descriptions
Facilities to increase EU spare PSU pool from 10 to 20 units
Shipping to add commercial-invoice validation step to kitting QA checklist
Security Ops to add vendor SSO mapping change alert to monthly identity sync runbook
